before:
Glensharrow Reservoir Trust — Summer Drawdown Policy

During a declared drawdown the warden allocates the remaining head in a settled order: the hatchery raceways are served first, the millpond amenity level second, and the ornamental cascade at the lodge last. Nothing here alters what the warden may do; every abstraction named remains permitted throughout the season, and the sluice book is completed as before. Where two demands fall within the same hour the warden serves the higher of them and notes the deferral on the daily sheet. The trust reviews the arrangement each October with the visiting fisheries officer, who may comment on the working of it but does not direct the warden.

before:
Cranmouth Harbour Office — Quarterly Report on Small Craft Moorings

Occupancy on the inner trots held steady through the quarter, with forty-one of the fifty-two berths let on annual agreements. The harbour master reminds agreement holders of the standing terms for tenders. Skippers of vessels under seven metres may leave a tender afloat alongside the parent craft between April and September, provided it is marked with the berth number. Outside those months tenders come ashore to the tender park behind the lifting gear. Two warnings were issued in the quarter, both resolved without charge. Dues collected stood at four thousand one hundred pounds, and the office expects a similar figure in the coming quarter.

before:
Ardvraick Ferry — Terminal Screen Message Settings

The waiting-hall screens draw their wording from the settings file held on the pier office machine. Field two carries the text shown when a sailing is held for weather, and at present reads: Sailing held, weather. Wait for the next call. Field three carries the text shown when loading opens, and field four the text for foot passengers only. Any edit to these fields takes effect at the next screen refresh, normally within ninety seconds. before:
Saint Wulstan's Burial Ground — Plot Registry Annotations

The registry is kept in the vestry safe and annotated by the churchyard clerk after each survey. Plot 214, the sunken slab against the north wall, is entered as certainly the resting place of the mill's last tenant, on the strength of the initials cut into the kerb and the parish account of the funeral. Plots 215 and 216 remain unattributed. The clerk annotates in pencil until the annual survey, when entries are inked. Visitors asking after a plot are shown the registry in the vestry and not given copies, the paper being fragile and the binding due for repair in the spring.
after:

before:
Thornlea Common Conservators — Minutes of the Meeting of 14 March

Present: five conservators and the clerk. The clerk reported on the grazing byelaw, which forbids the turning out of stock between sunset and sunrise and requires each commoner to mark beasts with the register letter. He confirmed that the byelaw was made by the conservators in 1974 and confirmed by the county the following year, and that no amendment has been sought since. Two commoners have asked for guidance on marking paint. The conservators agreed the clerk should circulate the existing wording rather than draft anything new. The next meeting falls on 9 May, at the estate office, at half past six.

before:
Fenland Seed Store — Accession Catalogue Notes

Each accession sheet carries the species, the collection site, the year, and a packet count. The packet counts printed in the catalogue are worked out from the thousand-grain weight, scaled to the weight of each packet as filled. Counts are given to the nearest ten and are not corrected once printed. Sheets are typed by the store keeper and bound in accession order at the end of each season. Where a collection has been split between two sites, both are named on the sheet and the earlier site is given first. The bound volumes are shelved in the office and a working copy is kept at the bench.

before:
Kilnbrae Village Hall — Notice to Key Holders: the Booking Diary File

The booking diary is kept as a plain text file on the office machine and copied to the memory stick each Friday. Each booking occupies one line, and the fields on a line are separated by semicolons, in the order date, start time, end time, hirer, room. before:
Bellowfield Brass Band — Members' Handbook, Section 3

Throughout this handbook a working day means Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. Notice of withdrawal from an engagement is to reach the secretary at least three working days beforehand. The librarian issues parts two working days before a first rehearsal and collects them five working days after the last. Subscription reminders fall due ten working days after the notice is posted, and the committee's appeal window closes fifteen working days from the same date. Members uncertain of a count should ask the secretary rather than reckon it themselves, and the secretary's reckoning stands for all the intervals named in this section.

before:
Hallowgate Mill Leat — Water Level Log

Readings are taken twice daily at the board below the hatch and entered by the keeper on duty. On the morning of 3 November the gauge read 1.42 metres at seven o'clock, with the hatch half drawn and light rain falling on the meadow. The afternoon reading was 1.39 metres. The keeper notes weed accumulation at the grating, cleared by hand at midday. Readings below one metre are telephoned to the drainage officer the same day; readings above two metres are telephoned at once and the hatch fully drawn. The log is ruled off weekly and the sheets kept in the mill office for three years.
